blocks.text: What Lazur does inside Notion on Mac

Lazur is a voice assistant that lives in the notch of your Mac. You hold ⌥⌘ and ask a question. Lazur looks at your screen only while you hold the keys, then answers out loud. It works in any Mac app, so you do not have to copy text into a chatbot first. In Notion, that means you can ask about the page you are looking at.

In Notion, most requests fall into five groups. You can ask Lazur to explain what is on screen, point at a control, walk you through a feature, draft text at the cursor, or take dictation. Each group needs a different kind of answer. Here is what each one looks like on a real page.

items: Explain: ask what a page, table or comment says. Lazur reads what is visible and answers out loud.
Point: ask where a control is. Lazur draws a circle and a label around it on your screen.
Guide: ask for steps. Lazur gives one click at a time and waits before the next one.
Draft: ask for a first version of text. Lazur types it at your cursor.
Dictate: hold fn and speak. Lazur types clean, formatted text where your cursor sits.

blocks.text: Notion on Mac requirements to check first

Start with the Mac. Notion's official help page says the desktop app needs macOS 13 or above. It also advises the latest version of your operating system for the best experience. The page lists no chip, memory or disk requirement for the Mac app. So the macOS version is the one hard check on that page.

blocks.title: Check your macOS version
blocks.text: Open the Apple menu and choose About This Mac. Read the macOS line. If it is older than macOS 13, update macOS before you install Notion's desktop app.

If you use Notion in a browser instead, the same help page lists browser support for web use. It names the last two major releases of Safari, Firefox and Edge. It names the last eight major Extended stable releases of Chrome. Lazur works the same way in either case, because it looks at whatever is on your screen.
Where people get stuck in Notion

Notion's help center groups its articles into categories such as Get started, Create & format pages, Build databases and Share & collaborate. Its featured topics are Getting started, Notion AI, Custom Agents, Notion Credits, Sharing & permissions and Databases. The page shows no view counts. So it cannot tell you which tasks people search for most. What the official pages do show are hard limits. Those limits are the most solid place to start, because Notion wrote them down.
These limits are worth knowing before you build a workflow around search or uploads.

items: Search skips comments and discussions. ⌘P will not find a word that only lives in a comment.
Workspace search does not look at select and multi-select tag values. Database search can find them.
Search skips most @mentions of pages and people.
Free uploads are capped at 5 MB per file. Paid plans allow 5 GB per file.
Page history is 7 days on the Free plan, and 30 days on Plus and Business.
A free workspace with two or more members can add a limited number of blocks. Notion does not state the number.

blocks.text: Find pages and text with search and shortcuts on Mac

Search is the first tool most people reach for. Press ⌘P to open search. Press ⌘K instead when your cursor is not inside a block. Notion's search help also says you can click Search at the top of the sidebar. To find a word on the page you are reading, press ⌘F. That search covers only the current page.

Here is a case that catches people out. You remember that a task had the tag Urgent, but you do not remember the page. Workspace search does not look at select and multi-select tag values, so ⌘P will not find it. Open the database instead and filter on the tag property. Database search can find tag values, so start there. Search finds pages. Filters find rows.

blocks.text: Ask Lazur where a control is on the page

Shortcuts only help when you know the name of the control. When you do not, ask. Hold ⌥⌘ and say, 'Where is the filter for this table?' Lazur draws a circle and a label around the control on your screen. You still click it. Lazur points. It does not press the button for you.

Describe the control by what it does, not by its icon. 'Where do I change who can see this page?' works better than 'where is the lock icon?' Lazur looks at the screen when you ask, so open the menu or panel you care about first. If the control is hidden behind a menu, open the menu and ask again.
Walk through a Notion feature one click at a time
For a longer task, ask for a walkthrough. Lazur gives one step, then waits for your click before it gives the next. Here is how a run looks when you want a filter on a database view.

items: Say: 'Walk me through adding a filter to this table.' Lazur points at the filter control.
Click it. Lazur waits, then names the next control, such as the property you want to filter on.
Pick the property and the value. Say 'next' when you are ready for the following step.
If a step does not match your screen, say so. Lazur looks at the screen again before it answers.

blocks.text: Draft text at the cursor in Notion

Drafting is a good fit for Notion. You have a blank block, a purpose and a few facts. Ask Lazur for a first version. It types the text at your cursor. Read it before you keep it. A draft is a starting point for your page, not the final version.

Specific asks give better drafts. A request like 'Draft an agenda for a short planning call with the design team' gives Lazur the audience, the length and the purpose. 'Write an agenda' gives it almost nothing. Name the reader, the length and the decision you need. Then edit the result by hand.
Dictate with fn in Notion on Mac

Hold fn, speak, and let go. Lazur turns your speech into clean, formatted text and types it where your cursor sits. That works in Notion or any other Mac app. Dictation is included with Lazur. Snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots handle the parts you repeat.
Dictation mistakes to avoid

items: Dictating into the wrong block. Click the spot first, then hold fn.
Trusting names. Add names and product words to your personal dictionary before a meeting.
Dictating private details in a shared room. Anyone nearby can hear what you say out loud.
Retyping the same line each week. Save it as a snippet, such as your meeting link.

blocks.text: What Lazur does not do in Notion

Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for Notion. Lazur is made separately from Notion, and it works in any Mac app, not only in Notion. Notion AI is Notion's own assistant inside the app. Lazur is a separate tool, so the two can sit side by side on your screen.

blocks.title: Shortcuts can change between versions
blocks.text: A third-party tracker lists Notion desktop v7.42.1, dated November 4, 2026, with a macOS fix for the Command Search and Notion AI shortcuts. Notion's own releases page did not confirm that numbering. Check notion.com/releases if a shortcut stops working.
Privacy when you ask about a Notion page

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to produce an answer. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Still, think before you hold the keys. A shared page with a salary table or a private contact list is still on screen.
Next steps for a Notion on Mac setup

items: Confirm your Mac runs macOS 13 or above.
Check the release notes at notion.com/releases so you know the current desktop version.
Download Lazur from the [download page](/download) and open it once.
Hold ⌥⌘ and ask a simple question, such as 'What is on screen?'
Test dictation with fn in a scratch page before you use it in a meeting.
Compare plans on the [pricing page](/pricing) before your trial ends.

faq.question: Does Lazur work in Notion on Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur works in any Mac app, including the Notion desktop app. Notion's desktop app needs macOS 13 or above. Lazur runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about the Notion window, or hold fn to dictate into it.

faq.question: Is Lazur the same as Notion AI?
faq.answer: No. Notion AI is built into Notion. Lazur is a separate voice assistant for your Mac. It is not a plugin or add-in for Notion. It works in Notion and in other Mac apps alike.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons or change my Notion page?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at buttons, explains what is on screen and guides you one click at a time. It drafts and types text at your cursor when you ask or dictate. You make the changes you want to keep.

faq.question: Why won't ⌘P find a word that is in a comment?
faq.answer: Notion's search help says comments and discussions are not included in search results. Property values such as select and multi-select tags are not searched in workspace search either. Search inside the database to find tag values.

faq.question: How big a file can I upload to Notion for free?
faq.answer: Free users can upload images, videos and file attachments up to 5 MB each. Plus, Business and Enterprise plans allow files up to 5 GB each, according to Notion's pricing page. Check the pricing page again before you plan a large upload.

faq.question: Does Lazur store my screenshots?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to produce an answer. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: Do I need the latest macOS for Notion?
faq.answer: Notion's desktop app needs macOS 13 or above. Notion also advises the latest version of your operating system for the best experience. If your Mac runs an older macOS, update it before you install the app.
